Hi Avery —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and the next steps below. I attached a short evidence matrix + our redline draft to the MSA (RDW_MSA_redline_v1.docx).

Summary:
- SOC 2: attaching the 2024 Type II report (SOC2_2024_Report.pdf). Date range: 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31.
- Audit rights: we can accept a production-systems-only carveout and provide a scoped exhibit that limits inspection to named sub-systems and data flows. See clause suggestions in the attached redline.
- Pen test: we propose two standard windows — "Rolling" (monthly scheduling with 2-week notice) or "Fixed" (one 5-day window per quarter). For vendor testing we require ephemeral staging creds, an NDA, and a scannable target list; full details are in the proposed pen-test appendix in the redline.
- Evidence retention/redaction: we can provide sampled evidence for SOC2 assertions and an encrypted S3 share for requested artifacts. We will redact customer-sensitive PII from logs but will provide artifact proofs (checksums, redaction notes).

Action items (from Redwood):
1) Vanessa: legal and ops to review redline and mark anything that requires escalation to counsel.
2) Karthik: propose alternative wording for the inspection carveout that preserves limited forensic access for critical incidents.
3) Marissa (me): share SOC report (attached) and upload the evidence matrix to the drive link below.

Attachments: RDW_MSA_redline_v1.docx, evidence_matrix_acme_health.xlsx, SOC2_2024_Report.pdf

If you can confirm which pen-test cadence (Rolling vs Fixed) Acme prefers we can lock the language and get a DocuSign envelope over by EOD tomorrow.

Best,

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the draft. A few legal-level notes to reconcile before we send to counsel:

1) Scope language: the proposed production-systems-only carveout is fine, but we should add a short definition list (services, control planes, and the "public API" endpoints) and explicitly exclude third-party managed services. That keeps our supply-chain exposure limited.

2) Notice and remediation: for any on-site / vendor-led pen test we should keep a mandatory 48-hour emergency stop and a mutually agreed remediation SLA for high-severity findings. I added suggested wording in RDW_MSA_redline_v1 (comments).

3) Evidence delivery: offering an encrypted S3 share is good. Add an optional scheduled evidence snapshot (quarterly) rather than open ad-hoc pulls; customers can request adhoc pulls but those will require additional redaction and be charged as professional services.

4) Escalation: if Acme requires broader inspection scope we should route to Legal + Security for one-off exceptions and capture in a written addendum (to avoid setting precedent).

I am available for a quick legal sync at 2pm PT if we want to run counsel through the current redline.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
